questions.question: 1. In predator–prey interactions, satiation refers to:

answers.a: The maximum growth rate of the prey
answers.b: The point at which predators are no longer motivated to hunt additional prey

questions.question: 2. According to the theory, increasing the prey carrying capacity generally has what effect on predators?

answers.b: Increases the likelihood that predators reach satiation

questions.question: 3. Which parameter in the simulator represents the carrying capacity of the prey population?
4. During the simulation, if the predator population reaches satiation while prey availability continues to increase, what is the most likely outcome?

answers.a: Predation rate continues increasing without limit
answers.b: Predator feeding rate approaches a maximum despite increasing prey density

questions.question: 5. What is meant by the carrying capacity (K) of a prey population?

answers.a: The maximum number of predators an environment can support
answers.b: The maximum sustainable prey population supported by the environment
